title: Effectiveness of Counter-Speech against Abusive Content: A Multidimensional Annotation and Classification Study
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the effectiveness of counter-speech against online hate speech, with a significant portion of the data focusing on Islamophobic hate speech.
findings: The study's framework was applied to datasets including a large corpus of counter-speech against Islamophobia (CONAN). It found that expert-written counter-speech (from CONAN) scored higher on average effectiveness dimensions (Clarity, Evidence, Rebuttal, Fairness) than user-generated speech, while user-generated speech scored higher on emotional appeal. The models showed domain shift challenges when generalizing between the expert-written, Islamophobia-focused dataset and the more general user-written dataset, particularly for classifying emotional appeal.
